name: Frame Collective SynthMark Statement Longcoat
description:
The Frame Collective's flagship piece for synthetic identity declaration: a structured longcoat in matte silver-white syntex with deliberate proportioning for non-human body ratios — extended torso, widened shoulder math, and a hem engineered for digitigrade or elongated leg structures. The exterior is printed with the Synthetic Personhood Accord text in dense micro-type across every panel, readable only at close range. On the back, in large stamped letters: 'NOT PROPERTY.'

Lapels carry embedded chromatic strips that cycle through colors impossible to reproduce in natural human skin tone — a deliberate declaration of synthetic difference as beauty, not deficit. Sold only to verified synthetic individuals through Frame Collective's encrypted distribution network.
functionality: Proportioned for synthetic body ratios including digitigrade legs and non-standard torso lengths; chromatic lapel strips are BCI-addressable and can be set to display personal identity data; magnetic closures function without fine motor precision.
what_it_says: I am synthetic, I am here, and I dressed this morning in an act of political self-determination.
story_hooks: A human is caught wearing one fraudulently — the Frame Collective wants an explanation, and the synthetic community is divided between anger and curiosity about why.
A corponation legal team has filed to have the Synthetic Personhood Accord text classified as 'incitement' — making the coat itself potentially illegal to wear in corporate zones.
A synthetic wearing this coat in a Tier 4 lobby is detained by CorpSec; what happens next depends entirely on who's watching.
